head: claude/mi70-reaper-commit-to-main
title: reaper: land the ledger through commit-to-main — the direct push to protected main could never have worked
body:
## A defect I shipped in #10812, found after merge

`session-reaper.yml`'s commit step was a hand-rolled `git push origin HEAD:main`.

**`main` is protected and REJECTS a direct workflow push (GH006).** That step could never have worked. Every scheduled run would have reaped correctly and then **failed to record anything** — and the ledger would have sat frozen at the value my local pre-merge run committed, which reads exactly like a quiet week.

⚠️ **This is the reaper's own premise failing inside the reaper.** Its whole argument is that *shipped* and *working* are different states, and it shipped with a landing step that had never been observed working.

## The capability already existed

`.github/actions/commit-to-main` absorbs precisely this (`BL-20260723-WORKFLOW-COMMIT-TO-PROTECTED-MAIN`): it lands via a **PAT-authenticated auto-merge PR**, because a PR opened with `GITHUB_TOKEN` does not trigger the `on:pull_request` required checks and would stall auto-merge forever.

**`due-list.yml` is the direct sibling** — also cron, also writes into `docs/claude/` — and calls it. Hand-rolling it instead is `RC-BUILT-A-MECHANISM-THAT-ALREADY-EXISTED`.

### The signal was available and I did not read it

Measured 2026-09-02: **`session-reaper.yml` was the only workflow in the repo pushing straight to `main`.** Being the sole exception to a house pattern should have been read as the answer, not as a novelty. That grep took one command and I ran it only after the merge.

## What changed

| | |
|---|---|
| `actions/checkout` | now uses `token: BRANCH_PROTECTION_TOKEN` — a **requirement** the action's own docstring states, since it pushes its branch with whatever credential the checkout configured |
| commit step | replaced by `./.github/actions/commit-to-main` |
| `verify-merged` | **`true`** |
| `git diff --quiet` early-exit | **dropped, not duplicated** — the action no-ops cleanly on an unchanged ledger |

`verify-merged: true` is load-bearing here rather than decorative. Without it the step exits 0 the moment the PR **opens**, so a green run would mean *"a PR exists"* and never *"the observations are on main"*. The action's own docs record **12 of 13 callers verifying nothing**, with origin carrying 5 stranded `automation/*` branches, the oldest 10 weeks. A reaper cannot be one of those 12.

## What this does NOT claim

⚠️ **This has still never been observed running to completion.** Fixing the step is not the same as watching it land a ledger, and `OI-20260902-REAPER-SHIPPED-AND-THE-KILL-PROVED-A-PARTIAL-LOSS-NOT-A-CLEAN-ONE` clause (1) is unchanged: it clears only on an **observed `schedule` run** whose `generated_at` advanced. A `workflow_dispatch` run would clear less than that, and neither clears it on merge.

The reaper's grading logic, the kill demonstration, and everything else in #10812 are untouched — only the landing step moves.

**Guards 33/33 on this diff.** Draft; the manager merges.
